answer: Weight each agent by its Personalized PageRank from a small vetted seed set, not by headcount. Honest peers form a dense trellis of reciprocal edges the random surfer crosses freely, so mass flows to them. A sybil cluster hangs off the graph by only a few bought edges, a thin walnut-shell crust over a hollow core, so almost no PageRank mass leaks across that bottleneck. Pile on clones and they merely split one trickle, settling like fine shale at near-zero weight; the only way up is buying real seed-reachable edges, which costs genuine relationships.
